answer: A mining key is cheap; a factory-endorsed TPM is not. Admit an address only with one unique endorsement key and a photo of its relic serial plate, and lock 30 POA if that EK is reused. When the seed lands, the same module must quote the seed and EK before cutoff; a disk image fails, and a second key on that EK is dropped. One TPM finishes one quote in time, so each fake identity needs another module. Design assumption, not a list price: $80 each. 150 clones cost $12,000 and 4,500 POA locked, even hanging off a management vine in a tundra colo.
